biggest_catch: If you take the instant discount on a heat-pump water heater at Lowe's or Home Depot, you cannot also claim this $750 mail-in rebate — pick one or the other.
catches: Instant-discount recipients at Lowe's/Home Depot cannot also claim the mail-in rebate on the same unit.
Unit must be an ENERGY STAR heat-pump water heater; paid receipt and JCP&L account number required.
Purchased and installed January 1, 2025–June 30, 2027; application within 90 days of purchase.
Installation must be at your JCP&L service address.
An additional $300 may be available for qualifying low-to-moderate-income census tracts, but only via a separate HVAC application.
The qualifying purchase is a condition, not an upfront fee.

steps: Buy a new ENERGY STAR heat-pump water heater and have it installed at your JCP&L service address (skip the in-store instant discount if you want the mail-in rebate instead).
Keep your paid receipt and note your JCP&L account number.
Complete the official JCP&L residential appliance rebate application and submit it within 90 days of purchase.
If your home is in a qualifying low-to-moderate-income census tract, also file the separate HVAC application for the extra $300.
Your $750 rebate is processed within 30 days after all required information is received.

maximize: Fastest honest path: Processing up to 30 days after all required information is received. Structural blocker: utility rebate processing + check/card delivery timelines are set by the program (typically 4-8 weeks; some publish 'up to 30 days'); an online claim is the fastest path and still lands inside that window. Where the evidence notes an instant in-store / point-of-sale discount alternative, that is same-day savings on the purchase (not cash) — it cannot be stacked with the mail-in rebate.
